title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 76 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 459–462 (Night 76, continuing directly from nights-75), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 76 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The stoker, seized by the chamberlain’s servant and his boys, expects the worst but is secretly treated with honour; the caravan nears Baghdad and meets the vizier Dandān’s army, which brings the chamberlain news that King ʿUmar has died by poison and that the nobles mean to send for his sons. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالسَّبْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-sabʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the sixth and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-sixth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَقَّادَ لَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَشُدَّ حِمَارَهُ وَيَهْرُبَ وَصَارَ يُكَلِّمُ نَفْسَهُ وَيَقُولُ يَا تُرَى كَيْفَ حَالُهُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-waqqāda lammā arāda an yashudda ḥimārahu wa-yahruba wa-ṣāra yukallimu nafsahu wa-yaqūlu yā turā kayfa ḥāluhu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the stoker, when he wanted to tie-up his donkey and flee, began speaking to his self and saying: O see-now, how is his state?
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the stoker, when he was about to saddle his donkey and flee, began talking to himself and saying, “I wonder how he is faring.”
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words. يا ترى is a set phrase, “I wonder”.

sentences.t: فَمَاتَمَّ كَلَامُهُ إِلَّا وَالْخَادِمُ وَاقِفٌ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَالْغِلْمَانُ حَوْلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā tamma kalāmuhu illā wa-al-khādimu wāqifun ʿalā raʾsihi wa-al-ghilmānu ḥawlahu
sentences.l: And his speech was not complete except-that the servant was standing at his head and the boys around him.
sentences.i: He had hardly finished speaking when there was the servant, standing over him with the boys all around.
sentences.n: The print runs ما تم into one word (فماتم).

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ الْوَقَّادُ فَرَأَى الْخَادِمَ وَاقِفاً عَلَى رَأْسِهِ فَارْتَعَدَتْ فَرَائِصُهُ وَخَافَ وَقَالَ وَقَدْ رَفَعَ صَوْتَهُ بِالْكَلَامِ إِنَّهُ مَا عَرَفَ مِقْدَارَ مَا عَمِلْتُهُ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمَعْرُوفِ فَأَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ غَمَزَ الْخَادِمَ وَهَؤُلَاءِ الْغِلْمَانَ عَلَيَّ وَأَنَّهُ أَشْرَكَنِي مَعَهُ فِى الذَّنْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata al-waqqādu fa-raʾā al-khādima wāqifan ʿalā raʾsihi fa-irtaʿadat farāʾiṣuhu wa-khāfa wa-qāla wa-qad rafaʿa ṣawtahu bi-al-kalāmi innahu mā ʿarafa miqdāra mā ʿamiltuhu maʿahu mina al-maʿrūfi fa-aẓunnu annahu ghamaza al-khādima wa-hāʾulāʾi al-ghilmāna ʿalayya wa-annahu ashrakanī maʿahu fī al-dhanbi
sentences.l: And the stoker turned and saw the servant standing at his head, and his rib-muscles trembled and he feared, and he said, having raised his voice in the speech: Truly he did not know the measure of what I did with him of the kindness, so I think that he has winked to the servant and these boys against me, and that he has made me share with him in the offence.
sentences.i: The stoker turned and saw the servant standing over him; his flesh quaked and he was afraid, and, raising his voice, he said, “He has no sense of all the kindness I showed him! I suppose he has signalled the servant and these boys against me, and has made me his partner in the crime.”
sentences.n: The stoker speaks half to himself, loudly enough to be heard. فرائص are the muscles beside the chest, which tremble with fear.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْخَادِمِ صَاحَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ مَنِ الَّذِي كَانَ يُنْشِدُ الْأَشْعَارَ يَا كَذَّابُ كَيْفَ تَقُولُ لِي أَنَا مَا أَنْشَدْتُ الْأَشْعَارَ وَلَاعْرِفُ مَنْ أَنْشَدَهَا وَهُوَ رَفِيقُكَ فَأَنَا لَا أُفَارِقُكَ مِنْ هُنَا إِلَى بَغْدَادَ وَالَّذِي يَجْرِي عَلَى رَفِيقِكَ يَجْرِي عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-khādimi ṣāḥa ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu mani alladhī kāna yunshidu al-ashʿāra yā kadhdhābu kayfa taqūlu lī anā mā anshadtu al-ashʿāra wa-lāʿrifu man anshadahā wa-huwa rafīquka fa-anā lā ufāriquka min hunā ilā baghdāda wa-alladhī yajrī ʿalā rafīqika yajrī ʿalayka
sentences.l: And behold, with the servant: he shouted at him and said to him: Who is the one who was reciting the poems, O liar? How do you say to me: I did not recite the poems and I do not know who recited them, and he is your companion? For I will not part from you from here to Baghdad, and that-which runs upon your companion runs upon you.
sentences.i: Suddenly the servant was shouting at him: “Who was it that was reciting poetry, you liar? How can you tell me, ‘I did not recite the poems and I do not know who did’? He is your companion! I shall not leave you from here to Baghdad, and whatever befalls your companion will befall you.”
sentences.n: The print writes ولاعرف for ولا أعرف, one alif doing the work of two. The servant answers a denial the stoker has not actually spoken; the speech is best read as the servant’s scornful pretence of what the stoker will say.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَقَّادُ كَلَامَهُ قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مَا خِفْتُ مِنْهُ وَقَعْتُ فِيهِ ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَ هَذَا الْبَيْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-waqqādu kalāmahu qāla fī nafsihi mā khiftu minhu waqaʿtu fīhi thumma anshada hādhā al-bayta
sentences.l: And when the stoker heard his speech he said in his self: What I feared of it I have fallen into; then he recited this verse:
sentences.i: When the stoker heard this he said to himself, “What I feared, I have fallen into.” Then he recited this verse:

sentences.t: كَانَ الَّذِي خِفْتُ انْ يَكُّوْنَا * اِنَّا اِلَى اللَّهِ رَاجِعُوْنَا
sentences.tr: kāna alladhī khiftu an yakūnā * innā ilā allāhi rājiʿūnā
sentences.l: There-was that which I feared would be; * truly we, to God, are returning.
sentences.i: What I feared would come to pass has come to pass; * we belong to God, and to Him we return.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. The shadda in يكّونا is the print’s; the second half echoes Qurʾān 2:156.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَادِمَ صَاحَ عَلَى الْغِلْمَانِ وَقَالَ أَنْزِلُوهُ عَنِ الْحِمَارِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khādima ṣāḥa ʿalā al-ghilmāni wa-qāla anzilūhu ʿani al-ḥimāri
sentences.l: Then the servant shouted at the boys and said: Bring-him-down off the donkey.
sentences.i: Then the servant shouted to the boys, “Get him down off that donkey!”

sentences.t: فَأَنْزَلُوا الْوَقَّادَ عَنْ حِمَارِهِ وَأَتَوْا لَهُ بِحِصَانٍ فَرَكِبَهُ وَمَشَى صُحْبَةَ الرَّكْبِ وَالْغِلْمَانُ حَوْلَهُ مُحْدِقُونَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-anzalū al-waqqāda ʿan ḥimārihi wa-atawū lahu bi-ḥiṣānin fa-rakibahu wa-mashā ṣuḥbata al-rakbi wa-al-ghilmānu ḥawlahu muḥdiqūna bihi
sentences.l: So they brought-down the stoker from his donkey, and they came to him with a stallion, and he rode it and went in company of the caravan, the boys around him encircling him.
sentences.i: So they took the stoker down from his donkey and brought him a horse, which he mounted, and he rode along with the caravan, the boys ringed about him.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْخَادِمُ إِنْ عُدِمَ مِنْهُ شَعْرَةٌ كَانَتْ بِوَاحِدٍ مِنْكُمْ وَقَالَ سِرّاً أَكْرِمُوهُ وَلَا تُهِينُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahumu al-khādimu in ʿudima minhu shaʿratun kānat bi-wāḥidin minkum wa-qāla sirran akrimūhu wa-lā tuhīnūhu
sentences.l: And the servant said to them: If a hair is lost from him, it will be with one of you; and he said secretly: Honour him and do not insult him.
sentences.i: The servant told them, “If so much as a hair of his head is lost, one of you will answer for it.” Then he added in private, “Treat him with honour, and do not insult him.”
sentences.n: The second command is given in secret, so that the stoker, who thinks himself a prisoner, does not hear it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَاىٔ الْوَقَّادُ الْغِلْمَانَ حَوْلَهُ يَئِسَ مِنَ الْحَيَوةِ وَالْتَفَتَ إِلَى الْخَادِمِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا مُقَدَّمُ مَا أَنَا أَخُوةُ وَلَا قَرِيبُهُ وَهَذَا الشَّابُّ لَا يَقْرُبُ لِي وَلَا أَنَا أَقْرَبُ لَهُ وَإِنَّمَا أَنَا رَجُلٌ وَقَّادٌ فِي حَمَّامٍ وَوَجَدْتُهُ مُلْقِياً عَلَى الْمَزْبَلَةِ مَرِيضاً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-waqqādu al-ghilmāna ḥawlahu yaʾisa mina al-ḥayawati wa-iltafata ilā al-khādimi wa-qāla lahu yā muqaddamu mā anā akhūhu wa-lā qarībuhu wa-hādhā al-shābbu lā yaqrubu lī wa-lā anā aqrabu lahu wa-innamā anā rajulun waqqādun fī ḥammāmin wa-wajadtuhu mulqiyan ʿalā al-mazbalati marīḍan
sentences.l: And when the stoker saw the boys around him he despaired of life, and turned to the servant and said to him: O commander, I am not his brother nor his relative, and this youth is not near to me nor am I nearer to him; rather I am a man, a stoker in a bath-house, and I found him thrown on the rubbish-heap, ill.
sentences.i: When the stoker saw the boys around him he gave up hope of life. He turned to the servant and said, “Captain, I am not his brother or his kinsman; this young man is nothing to me, nor I to him. I am only a stoker in a bathhouse, and I found him lying sick on the rubbish heap.”
sentences.n: The print has the tā’ marbūṭa in اخوة where the pronoun ـه is meant; it is read akhūhu, “his brother”. The print’s الحيوة (for الحياة) is kept.

sentences.t: وَسَارَ الرَّكْبُ وَالْوَقَّادُ يَبْكِي وَيَحْسِبُ فِي نَفْسِهِ أَلْفَ حِسَابٍ وَالْخَادِمُ مَاشٍ بِجَانِبِهِ وَلَمْ يُعَرِّفْهُ بِشَيْءٍ بَلْ يَقُولُ لَهُ قَدَا قَلَقْتَ سَيِّدَ تَنَا بِا نِشَادِ لِ الشِّعْرِ أَنْتَ وَهَذَا الصَّبِيَّى وَلَا تَخَافُ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ وَصَارَ الْخَادِمُ يَضْحَكُ عَلَيْهِ سِرّاً
sentences.tr: wa-sāra al-rakbu wa-al-waqqādu yabkī wa-yaḥsibu fī nafsihi alfa ḥisābin wa-al-khādimu māshin bi-jānibihi wa-lam yuʿarrifhu bi-shayʾin bal yaqūlu lahu qadā qalaqta sayyida tanā bi-ā nishādi li al-shiʿri anta wa-hādhā al-ṣabiyya wa-lā takhāfu ʿalā nafsika wa-ṣāra al-khādimu yaḍḥaku ʿalayhi sirran
sentences.l: And the caravan went on, and the stoker weeping and reckoning in his self a thousand reckonings, and the servant walking at his side; and he did not let him know anything, but says to him: You-have-troubled our lady with reciting of the poetry, you and this boy, and do not fear for yourself. And the servant kept laughing at him in secret.
sentences.i: The caravan went on, the stoker weeping and turning over a thousand reckonings in his mind, the servant walking beside him and telling him nothing. All he said was, “You have troubled our lady with your recitation of poetry, you and this boy — but do not fear for yourself.” And the servant kept laughing at him in secret.
sentences.n: The print breaks this speech into fragments (قدا قلقت سيد تنا با نشاد ل الشعر). It is read as لقد أقلقت سيدتنا بإنشاد الشعر, “you have disturbed our lady by reciting poetry”; “our lady” is Nuzhat al-Zamān, the chamberlain’s wife, in the litter. The stray ى at the end of الصبيى is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا نَزَلُوا أَتَاهُمُ الطَّعَامُ فَيَأْكُلُ هُوَ وَالْوَقَّادُ فِي آنِيَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَإِذَا أَكَلُوا أَمَرَ الْخَادِمُ الْغِلْمَانَ أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِقُلَّةِ سُكَّرٍ فَيَشْرَبُ مِنْهَا وَيُعْطِيهَا لِلْوَقَّادِ فَيَشْرَبُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā nazalū atāhumu al-ṭaʿāmu fa-yaʾkulu huwa wa-al-waqqādu fī āniyatin wāḥidatin fa-idhā akalū amara al-khādimu al-ghilmāna an yaʾtū bi-qullati sukkarin fa-yashrabu minhā wa-yuʿṭīhā li-al-waqqādi fa-yashrabu
sentences.l: And when they alighted the food came to them, and he eats, he and the stoker, in one vessel; and when they had eaten the servant ordered the boys to bring a jug of sugar, and he drinks from it and gives it to the stoker, and he drinks.
sentences.i: Whenever they halted, food was brought, and the servant ate with the stoker from a single dish; and when they had finished he would order the boys to bring a jug of sugared water, drink from it himself, and pass it to the stoker, who drank.
sentences.n: قلة سكر is a jug of sweet drink (sherbet). The verbs shift to the present for the repeated action.

sentences.t: لَكِنَّهُ لَمْ تَنْشَفْ لَهُ دَمْعَةٌ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَالْحُزْنِ عَلَى فِرَاقِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَعَلَى مَا وَقَعَ لَهُمَا فِي غُرْبَتِهِمَا وَهُمَا سَائِرَانِ
sentences.tr: lākinnahu lam tanshaf lahu damʿatun mina al-khawfi ʿalā nafsihi wa-al-ḥuzni ʿalā firāqi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-ʿalā mā waqaʿa lahumā fī ghurbatihimā wa-humā sāʾirāni
sentences.l: But no tear of his dried, from fear for his self and sorrow at the parting of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and at what had befallen the two of them in their exile, while the two were travelling.
sentences.i: But not a tear of his dried, for fear of what might happen to him, and grief at being parted from Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and for all that had befallen the two of them in their exile as they journeyed.

sentences.t: وَالْحَاجِبُ تَارَةً يَكُونُ عَلَى بَابِ الْمَحَفَّةِ لِأَجْلِ خِدْمَةِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ بْنِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَأُخْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ وَتَارَةً يُلَاحِظُ الْوَقَّادَ وَنُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَأَخُوهَا ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ فِي حَدِيثٍ وَشَكْوَى وَلَمْ يَزَالَا عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ وَهُمْ سَائِرُونَ حَتَّى قَرُبُوا مِنَ الْبِلَادِ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْبِلَادِ إِلَّا ثَلَثَةُ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ḥājibu tāratan yakūnu ʿalā bābi al-maḥaffati li-ajli khidmati ḍawʾi al-makāni bni al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni wa-ukhtihi nuzhati al-zamāni wa-tāratan yulāḥiẓu al-waqqāda wa-nuzhatu al-zamāni wa-akhūhā ḍawʾu al-makāni fī ḥadīthin wa-shakwā wa-lam yazālā ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati wa-hum sāʾirūna ḥattā qarubū mina al-bilādi wa-lam yabqa baynahum wa-bayna al-bilādi illā thalathatu ayyāmin
sentences.l: And the chamberlain at one time would be at the door of the litter for the service of Ḍawʾ al-Makān son of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and at another would watch the stoker, while Nuzhat al-Zamān and her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān were in talk and complaint; and the two did not cease in that state while they were travelling, until they drew near to the land, and there did not remain between them and the land except three days.
sentences.i: The chamberlain would sometimes wait at the door of the litter to serve Ḍawʾ al-Makān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and sometimes keep an eye on the stoker, while Nuzhat al-Zamān and her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān sat talking and lamenting. So they went on until they drew near their own country, with only three days left between them and Baghdad.
sentences.n: The print has ثلثة for ثلاثة, “three”. “The land” (البلاد) is Baghdad and its territory, as the sequel shows. The print’s ولم يزالا is dual, “the two of them”, the brother and sister.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلُوا وَقْتَ الْمَسَاءِ وَاسْتَرَا حُوا وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا نَازِلِينَ إِلَى أَنْ لَاحَ الْفَجْرُ فَاسْتَيْقَظُوا وَأَرَادُوا أَنْ يَحْمِلُوا
sentences.tr: fa-nazalū waqta al-masāʾi wa-istarā ḥū wa-lam yazālū nāzilīna ilā an lāḥa al-fajru fa-istayqaẓū wa-arādū an yaḥmilū
sentences.l: So they alighted at the time of evening and rested, and did not cease being alighted until the dawn appeared; then they woke and wanted to load.
sentences.i: They halted in the evening and rested, and stayed encamped until the dawn showed; then they woke and made ready to load up and move on.
sentences.n: The print splits واستراحوا into two words (واسترا حوا).

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِغُبَارٍ عَظِيمٍ قَدْ لَاحَ لَهُمْ وَأَظْلَمَ الْجَّوُّ مِنْهُ حَتَّى صَارَكَا لَلَّيْلِ الدَّاجِي فَصَاحَ الْحَاجِبُ قَائِلاً أَمْهِلُوا وَلَا تَحْمِلُوا وَرَكِبَ هُوَ وَمَمَالِيكُهُ وَسَارُوا نَحْوَ ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ghubārin ʿaẓīmin qad lāḥa lahum wa-aẓlama al-jawwu minhu ḥattā ṣāraka li-al-layli al-dājī fa-ṣāḥa al-ḥājibu qāʾilan amhilū wa-lā taḥmilū wa-rakiba huwa wa-mamālīkuhu wa-sārū naḥwa dhālika al-ghubāri
sentences.l: And behold, a great dust had appeared to them, and the air grew dark from it until it became like the dusky night; and the chamberlain shouted, saying: Wait, and do not load! And he rode, he and his mamluks, and they went toward that dust.
sentences.i: Suddenly a great cloud of dust rose before them, and the air went so dark that it was like deepest night. The chamberlain cried out, “Wait! Do not load!” and he and his mamluks mounted and rode toward the dust.
sentences.n: The print has a shadda on the jīm of الجّو and splits كالليل as صاركا لليل; both are read by sense.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبُوا مِنْهُ بَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ عَسْكَرٌ جَرَّارٌ كَالْبَحْرِ الزَّخَّارِ وَفِيهِ رَايَاتٌ وَأَعْلَامٌ وَطُبُولٌ وَفُرْسَانٌ وَأَبْطَالٌ فَتَعَجَّبَ الْحَاجِبُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubū minhu bāna min taḥtihi ʿaskarun jarrārun ka-al-baḥri al-zakhkhāri wa-fīhi rāyātun wa-aʿlāmun wa-ṭubūlun wa-fursānun wa-abṭālun fa-taʿajjaba al-ḥājibu min amrihim
sentences.l: And when they drew near to it there appeared from beneath it a dragging army, like the swelling sea, and in it banners and standards and drums and horsemen and heroes; and the chamberlain wondered at their affair.
sentences.i: As they drew near, there appeared beneath it a vast, trailing host, like a swelling sea, with banners and standards, drums, horsemen and champions; and the chamberlain wondered at what it could mean.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَهُمُ الْعَسْكَرُ افْتَرَقَتْ مِنْهُ فِرْقَةٌ قَدْرُ خَمْسِمِائَةِ فَارِسٍ وَأَتَوْا إِلَى الْحَاجِبِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ وَأَحَاطُوا بِهِمْ وَأَحَاطَتْ كُلُّ خَمْسَةٍ بِمَمْلُوكٍ مِنْ مَمَالِيكِ الْحَاجِبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾahumu al-ʿaskaru iftaraqat minhu firqatun qadru khamsimiʾati fārisin wa-atawā ilā al-ḥājibi wa-man maʿahu wa-aḥāṭū bihim wa-aḥāṭat kullu khamsatin bi-mamlūkin min mamālīki al-ḥājibi
sentences.l: And when the army saw them, a troop separated from it, about five hundred horsemen, and they came to the chamberlain and those with him and surrounded them, and every five surrounded one mamluk of the chamberlain’s mamluks.
sentences.i: When the army saw them, a troop of some five hundred horsemen broke away and rode up to the chamberlain and his company and surrounded them, every five riders closing in on one of his mamluks.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْحَاجِبُ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ الْخَبَرُ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هَذِهِ الْعَسَاكِرُ حَتَّى تَفْعَلُ مَعَنَا هَذِهِ الْأَفْعَالَ فَقَالُوا لَهُ مَنْ أَنْتَ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ أَتَيْتَ وَإِلَى أَيْنَ تَتَوَجَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-ḥājibu ayyu shayʾin al-khabaru wa-min ayna hādhihi al-ʿasākiru ḥattā tafʿalu maʿanā hādhihi al-afʿāla fa-qālū lahu man anta wa-min ayna atayta wa-ilā ayna tatawajjahu
sentences.l: And the chamberlain said to them: What thing is the news, and from where are these armies, that they do with us these deeds? And they said to him: Who are you, and from where have you come, and to where are you heading?
sentences.i: The chamberlain said to them, “What is this? Whose armies are these, that they treat us so?” They answered, “Who are you, where have you come from, and where are you bound?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ أَنَا حَاجِبُ أَمِيرِ دِمَشْقَ الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانَ بْنِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ صَاحِبِ بَغْدَادَ وَأَرْضِ خُرَاسَانَ وَأَتَيْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ بِالْخَرَاجِ وَالْهَدِيَّةِ مُتَوَجِّهاً إِلَى وَالِدِهِ بِبَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum anā ḥājibu amīri dimashqa al-maliki sharkāna bni al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni ṣāḥibi baghdāda wa-arḍi khurāsāna wa-ataytu min ʿindihi bi-al-kharāji wa-al-hadiyyati mutawajjihan ilā wālidihi bi-baghdāda
sentences.l: And he said to them: I am the chamberlain of the governor of Damascus, the king Sharkān son of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, lord of Baghdad and the land of Khurasan; and I have come from him with the tribute and the gift, heading to his father at Baghdad.
sentences.i: He said, “I am the chamberlain of the governor of Damascus, King Sharkān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, lord of Baghdad and the land of Khurasan. I have come from him with the tribute and a gift, on my way to his father in Baghdad.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعُوا كَلَامَهُ أَرْخَوْا مَنَادِيلَهُمْ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ وَبَكَوْا وَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ قَدْمَاتَ وَمَا مَاتَ إِلَّا مَسْمُوماً فَتَوَجَّهْ وَمَا عَلَيْكَ بَأْسٌ حَتَّى تَجْتَمِعَ بِوَزِيرِهِ الْأَكْبَرِ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿū kalāmahu arkhaw manādīlahum ʿalā wujūhihim wa-bakaw wa-qālū lahu inna ʿumara bna al-nuʿmāni qadmāta wa-mā māta illā masmūman fa-tawajjah wa-mā ʿalayka baʾsun ḥattā tajtamiʿa bi-wazīrihi al-akbari al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: And when they heard his speech they let down their kerchiefs over their faces and wept, and said to him: ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān has died, and he did not die except poisoned; so go on, and there is no harm upon you until you meet his greatest vizier, the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: When they heard him they drew their kerchiefs down over their faces and wept, and said, “ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān is dead, and he died only by poison. Go on; no harm will come to you, until you meet his chief vizier, the vizier Dandān.”
sentences.n: The print runs قد مات into one word (قدمات). Letting the kerchief fall over the face is a sign of mourning.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْحَاجِبُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ بَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيداً وَقَالَ يَا خَيْبَتَنَا فِي هَذِهِ السَّفْرَةِ وَصَارَ يَبْكِي هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ إِلَى أَنِ اخْتَلَطُوا بِالْعَسْكَرِ فَاسْتَأْذَنُوا لَهُ مِنَ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ فَأَذِنَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ḥājibu dhālika al-kalāma bakā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-qāla yā khaybatanā fī hādhihi al-safrati wa-ṣāra yabkī huwa wa-man maʿahu ilā ani ikhtalaṭū bi-al-ʿaskari fa-istaʾdhanū lahu mina al-wazīri dandāna fa-adhina lahu
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain heard that speech he wept a violent weeping and said: O our disappointment in this journey! And he went on weeping, he and those with him, until they mingled with the army; and they asked leave for him from the vizier Dandān, and he gave him leave.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain heard this he wept bitterly and cried, “Alas for our failure on this journey!” He and his men went on weeping until they were among the army; then permission was asked for him from the vizier Dandān, and it was granted.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ الْوَزِيرُ بِضَرْبِ خِيَامِهِ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى سَرِيرٍ فِي وَسَطِ الْخَيْمَةِ وَأَمَرَ الْحَاجِبَ بِالْجُلُوسِ فَلَمَّا جَلَسَ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ خَبَرِهِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ أَنَّهُ حَاجِبُ أَمِيرِ دِمَشْقَ وَقَدْ جَاءَ بِالْهَدَايَا وَخَرَاجِ دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: wa-amara al-wazīru bi-ḍarbi khiyāmihi wa-jalasa ʿalā sarīrin fī wasaṭi al-khaymati wa-amara al-ḥājiba bi-al-julūsi fa-lammā jalasa saʾalahu ʿan khabarihi fa-aʿlamahu annahu ḥājibu amīri dimashqa wa-qad jāʾa bi-al-hadāyā wa-kharāji dimashqa
sentences.l: And the vizier commanded the striking of his tents, and sat on a couch in the middle of the tent and commanded the chamberlain to sit; and when he sat he asked him about his news, and he informed him that he was the chamberlain of the governor of Damascus and had come with the gifts and the tribute of Damascus.
sentences.i: The vizier ordered his tents pitched and sat on a couch in the middle of the tent, and bade the chamberlain sit. When he had sat down, the vizier asked what his business was, and the chamberlain told him that he was the chamberlain of the governor of Damascus and had come with gifts and the tribute of Damascus.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ ذَلِكَ بَكَى عِنْدَ ذِكْرِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ قَدْمَاتَ مَسْمُوماً وَبِسَبَبِ مَوْتِهِ اخْتَلَفَ النَّاسُ فِي مَنْ يُوَلُّونَهُ بَعْدَهُ حَتَّى أَوْقَعُوا الْقَتْلَ فِي بَعْضِهِمْ وَلَكِنْ مَنَعَهُمْ عَنْ بَعْضِهِمُ الْأَكَابِرُ وَالْأَشْرَافُ وَالْقُضَاةُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru dandānu dhālika bakā ʿinda dhikri al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni thumma qāla lahu al-wazīru dandānu inna al-malika ʿumara bna al-nuʿmāni qadmāta masmūman wa-bi-sababi mawtihi ikhtalafa al-nāsu fī man yuwallūnahu baʿdahu ḥattā awqaʿū al-qatla fī baʿḍihim wa-lākin manaʿahum ʿan baʿḍihimu al-akābiru wa-al-ashrāfu wa-al-quḍātu al-arbaʿatu
sentences.l: And when the vizier Dandān heard that he wept at the mention of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān; then the vizier Dandān said to him: The king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān has died poisoned, and because of his death the people differed over whom they should set over them after him, until they brought killing upon some of them; but there restrained them from one another the great-ones and the nobles and the four judges.
sentences.i: When the vizier Dandān heard this he wept at the mention of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Then he said, “King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān is dead, poisoned; and on account of his death the people fell to quarrelling over whom to set up after him, until they were killing one another. But the grandees and nobles and the four judges held them back.”
sentences.n: The four judges are the heads of the four Sunni schools of law.

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقَ جَمِيعُ النَّاسِ عَلَى أَنَّ مَا أَشَارَبِهِ الْقُضَاةُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ لَايُخَالِفُهُمْ فِيهِ أَحَدٌ فَوَقَعَ الِاتِّفَاقُ عَلَى أَنَّنَا نَسِيرُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ وَنَقْصِدُ وَلَدَهُ الْمَلِكَ شَرْكَانَ وَنَأْتِي بِهِ وَنُسَلْطِنُّهُ عَلَى مَمْلَكَةِ أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqa jamīʿu al-nāsi ʿalā anna mā ashāra bihi al-quḍātu al-arbaʿatu lā yukhālifuhum fīhi aḥadun fa-waqaʿa al-ittifāqu ʿalā annanā nasīru ilā dimashqa wa-naqṣidu waladahu al-malika sharkāna wa-naʾtī bihi wa-nusalṭinnuhu ʿalā mamlakati abīhi
sentences.l: And all the people agreed that what the four judges pointed to, no one would oppose them in it; and agreement fell on this, that we go to Damascus and make for his son the king Sharkān and bring him and make him sultan over the kingdom of his father.
sentences.i: All the people agreed that whatever the four judges decided, no one would oppose them in it; and it was settled that we should travel to Damascus, seek out his son King Sharkān, bring him back, and make him sultan over his father’s kingdom.
sentences.n: The print runs اشار به and لا يخالفهم into single words.

sentences.t: وَفِيهِمْ جَمَاعَةٌ يُرِيدُونَ وَلَدَهُ الثَّانِيَ وَقَالُوا إِنَّهُ يُسَمَّى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ تُسَمَّى نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَكَانَا قَدْ تَوَجَّهَا إِلَى أَرْضِ الْحِجَازِ وَمَضَى لَهُمَا خَمْسُ سِنِينَ وَلَمْ يَقَعْ لَهُمَا أَحَدٌ عَلَى خَبَرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-fīhim jamāʿatun yurīdūna waladahu al-thāniya wa-qālū innahu yusammā ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-lahu ukhtun tusammā nuzhatu al-zamāni wa-kānā qad tawajjahā ilā arḍi al-ḥijāzi wa-maḍā lahumā khamsu sinīna wa-lam yaqaʿ lahumā aḥadun ʿalā khabarin
sentences.l: And among them is a group who want his second son, and they said that he is called Ḍawʾ al-Makān and that he has a sister called Nuzhat al-Zamān, and that the two had set out for the land of the Hijaz, and five years have passed for them and no one has come upon news of them.
sentences.i: Among them, though, is a party who want his other son. They say he is called Ḍawʾ al-Makān and has a sister called Nuzhat al-Zamān, and that the two set out for the Hijaz, and five years have gone by since, with no one finding any news of them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْحَاجِبُ ذَلِكَ عَلِمَ أَنَّ الْقَضِيَّةَ الَّتِي وَقَعَتْ لِزَوْجَتِهِ صَحِيحَةٌ فَاغْتَمَّ لِمَوْتِ السُّلْطَانِ غَمّاً عَظِيماً وَلَكِنَّهُ فَرِحَ فَرَحاً شَدِيداً وَخُصُوصاً بِمَجِيءِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ لِأَنَّهُ يَصِيرُ سُلْطَاناً بِبَغْدَادَ فِي مَكَانِ أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ḥājibu dhālika ʿalima anna al-qaḍiyyata allatī waqaʿat li-zawjatihi ṣaḥīḥatun fa-ightamma li-mawti al-sulṭāni ghamman ʿaẓīman wa-lākinnahu fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan wa-khuṣūṣan bi-majīʾi ḍawʾi al-makāni li-annahu yaṣīru sulṭānan bi-baghdāda fī makāni abīhi
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain heard that he knew that the affair that had happened to his wife was true, and he was grieved at the death of the sultan with a great grief, but he rejoiced with a violent joy, and especially at the coming of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, because he would become sultan in Baghdad in the place of his father.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain heard this he knew that what had happened to his wife was true. He grieved deeply for the sultan’s death, yet he rejoiced exceedingly, above all at the prospect of Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s coming, since he would become sultan in Baghdad in his father’s place.
sentences.n: “What had happened to his wife” is the story Nuzhat al-Zamān told him of who she and her brother are.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted tale unsaid.
